theme: 3 terms on finding text: a pattern for text, the part that saves a match, and writing the pattern as readable Swift code

terms.definition: A pattern that describes the shape of text, used to find or check matching strings.

terms.definition: A part of a regex inside parentheses that saves the text it matched so you can use it.

video.title: Regex, Capture Group & Regex Builder | Day 55
video.description:
Learn to explain regex in Swift: Regex, Capture Group & Regex Builder, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Regex - A pattern that describes the shape of text, used to find or check matching strings.
Capture Group - A part of a regex inside parentheses that saves the text it matched so you can use it.
Regex Builder - A way to write a regex as readable Swift code with names like `OneOrMore`, from the RegexBuilder module.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain regex in English?

dialogue.title: Random symbols?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, what is `id`? It looks like random symbols.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a Regex. It describes the shape of the text you want.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So it finds the word Order, then some digits?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. And the parentheses around the digits make a Capture Group.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is that why `m.1` gives 4521 without the word Order?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The Capture Group saves only the digits.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Honestly, this Regex is hard to read.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then try Regex Builder. You write the same pattern as Swift code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Regex Builder is longer, but new teammates can read it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. A Regex finds text, a Capture Group keeps a part, and Regex Builder makes it readable.
A Regex describes the shape of the text you want.
